summary: Explore a projection while retaining access to original vector relationships.
objective: Show an embedding dataset projected into 3D with point selection, metadata and an original-space distance inspector.
example_prompts: Show an embedding dataset projected into 3D with point selection, metadata and an original-space distance inspector.

entities.name: Points
entities.guidance: Use consistent glyph size unless explicitly encoding a field; stable IDs survive filtering.

entities.name: Selection
entities.guidance: Link selected point to original vector metadata and nearest-neighbor readout; avoid hover-only access.

entities.name: Projection frame
entities.guidance: Label axes as projection coordinates without invented semantic units; use restrained depth cues.

state_contract.model: Supplied vector matrix and IDs plus a recorded projection method, parameters, seed and output coordinates; no dataset is bundled.
state_contract.authority: One canonical model owns semantic values; derive geometry and labels from it. Keep presentation transforms separate.
actions: Select point and inspect original-space neighbors.

invariants: Projection coordinates never overwrite original vectors.
Distance readout identifies its metric and whether it is original or projected space.
Do not infer semantic categories or global distances from attractive clusters alone.
motion_guidance: Refitting is a deliberate action with a new projection revision; interpolation between fits is presentation only.
known_limits: Source abstract establishes 2D/3D projection purpose, not distance preservation or cluster truth.
Requires a real dataset and computed or supplied projection; random points must be labeled synthetic.
Authored guidance; no scene runtime or visual verification has run for this recipe.

claims.statement: t-SNE maps high-dimensional data points to positions in a two- or three-dimensional visualization.
claims.scope: Method purpose described by the original paper abstract; no preservation guarantee.
